resources.string: OneOS Probe
What the tests read, root and what is shared
OneOS Probe only reads

It runs read-only tests as root and packs what they find into a zip for the OneOS team. Nothing on the phone changes: root writes no file and sets no setting or property, and nothing is flashed or switched.
Root is needed
The tests run as root (KernelSU, Magisk or APatch). Allow OneOS Probe when your root manager asks; in KernelSU or APatch, allow it in the superuser list first.
Personal data is removed first

Before anything can be shared, OneOS Probe removes IMEI and MEID, serial numbers and device IDs, MAC addresses, SIM and phone numbers, emails, Wi-Fi and account names and locations. You can open every file before you share it.
You decide what is shared
The findings stay in the app until you share the zip or save it. OneOS Probe has no internet permission.
Switching is in the OneOS app
This app cannot prepare or switch to another OS. The findings tell the OneOS team whether the OneOS app can run on this phone.
I understand that the tests need root and only read
Read-only tests for the OneOS team
About OneOS Probe
The OneOS app checks everything again before it prepares or switches anything.
These facts come from Android APIs and system properties. OneOS Probe wrote nothing and ran nothing as root, except su -c id if you tapped Check root.
Waiting for root… allow OneOS Probe if your root manager asks.

OneOS Probe will run \"su -c id\" once. It only prints which user it runs as and changes nothing.\n\nMagisk may ask you to allow OneOS Probe. In KernelSU or APatch, allow OneOS Probe in the superuser list first.
Checking root… allow OneOS Probe if your root manager asks.

Every command only reads. Root writes no file, sets no property or setting and starts or stops nothing. The results go to OneOS Probe over a pipe and stay in its own storage until you share them. Tap a test below to see its exact command.

Before anything can be shared, OneOS Probe removes IMEI and MEID, serial numbers and device IDs, MAC addresses, SIM numbers (ICCID, IMSI), phone numbers, emails, Wi-Fi names, account names and locations. No logs, messages, contacts, photos or files are read. You can open every file before sharing.

OneOS Probe will run \"su -c id\" and then the read-only commands listed on this screen. Nothing on the phone is changed. The results stay in OneOS Probe until you share them, and personal data is removed before that.\n\nMagisk may ask you to allow OneOS Probe. In KernelSU or APatch, allow OneOS Probe in the superuser list first.
Removes the zip and the findings folder from OneOS Probe\'s storage.
About OneOS Probe

OneOS Probe is the read-only part of OneOS as an app of its own, for sharing findings: it checks this phone, runs the tests as root, removes personal data and builds a findings zip you can share. It cannot prepare or switch anything; that is the OneOS app. It installs next to OneOS and needs its own root grant.

Every root command is in the list on Run tests (tap a test to see it) and only reads; the app checks the list against its read-only rules before every run. Root writes no file, sets nothing and starts or stops nothing. Nothing leaves the phone unless you share it.
